title: Convert Sorted Array to Height-Balanced Binary Search Tree
statement:
You are given an array of unique integers arranged in strictly increasing order. Your task is to build a binary search tree from these values such that the resulting tree is height-balanced.

A binary search tree satisfies the property that for every node, all values in its left subtree are smaller and all values in its right subtree are larger. A tree is considered height-balanced when, for every node in the tree, the heights of its left and right subtrees differ by at most one.

Because several different height-balanced arrangements may satisfy the input, any valid tree that meets the balance and BST-ordering requirements should be accepted as a correct answer. Return the root node of the tree you construct.

Assume a standard binary tree node structure is available, where each node stores an integer value along with references to its left and right children.

examples.explanation: The middle element 8 becomes the root. The left half [2,4,6] and right half [10,12,14] are recursively converted the same way, producing 4 as the root of the left subtree (children 2 and 6) and 12 as the root of the right subtree (children 10 and 14). Every node's subtrees differ in height by at most 1, and an in-order traversal of the tree reproduces the original sorted array.

With an even number of elements, one valid choice picks 5 as the root (splitting into left half [1,3] and right half [7]). The right side has one node (7) directly as the right child, while the left side recursively places 1 as a left child with 3 attached as its right child, since 1 is smaller than 5. This keeps every subtree's height difference within 1, so the tree qualifies as balanced even though other equally valid balanced trees exist for this input.

constraints: nums is sorted in strictly increasing order (no duplicate values)
